column1: # Classification of every comment-hygiene hit fp-scan.py finds in this
# repository's own committed source. One record per hit, three tab-separated
# true_positive  the comment really does carry change history; the scanner is
#                right to flag it. Under this project's comment policy that
#                also makes it a comment the next task touching that file is
#                expected to rewrite -- the gate measures the SCANNER, not the
#                repository's compliance, so a true positive is not a defect
# false_positive the patterns misread ordinary prose. fp-report.sh fails while
#                any of these exist: a tell that reaches ordinary prose blocks
#                real writes mid-edit, which costs more than a missed
# The third field is the matched text as scanned. fp-report.sh compares it, so
# a line that shifts or is rewritten shows up as a stale entry rather than
# silently transferring its verdict to whatever now sits at that line number.
# and reconcile by hand. Every new key needs a human judgement; that is why
# this file is kept separate from the scan rather than produced by it.
# CodeRabbit review references, task-NN work-item references and version
# narration ("added in vX.Y.Z", "vX.Y.Z removes ...") are exactly the three
# mechanical tells the scanner claims to detect, and each hit below is one of
# them sitting in a full-line comment. None is a version naming a
# wire-compatibility contract, an ordinal in prose, a hex colour, or a URL path
# segment -- the four shapes the eval suite pins as non-matches.
